title: Input skip: lower MSE, same generator?
setting: Synthetic low-rank sinusoidal Gaussian data (32 coordinates, 4 latent factors, plus a mean offset) is fit with a small linear Gaussian VAE (8 latents, full-batch Adam, 400 steps, gradient clipping). Arms differ in the constant input skip alpha and in the observation variance, which is anchored to a PPCA noise estimate. The metric is the energy score of 256 generated samples against 200 held-out observations, per sqrt(dim). Diagnostics are held-out reconstruction MSE and exact Gaussian NLL per coordinate.

paper.title: An Input Skip Can Reparameterize a VAE Without Improving the Generator
paper.claim: A constant input skip lowers reconstruction MSE by b^2 but does not improve generative quality, and changing skip and observation variance together worsens energy score and NLL.

metric.name: energy_score
metric.description: Energy score of model samples versus held-out observations, averaged over test points and divided by sqrt(dim). Lower is better.

factors.name: method
factors.description: no_skip: alpha=0 at base (PPCA) observation variance. skip_same_var: skip alpha with the same observation variance, so residual variance is b^2 times base and the model is separately trained. skip_resid_var: skip alpha with residual variance kept at base, so observation variance is base/b^2, as in the paper's joint-change comparison.

factors.name: alpha
factors.description: Skip weight used by the skip arms (ignored by no_skip).

factors.name: noise_sd
factors.description: Standard deviation of the true observation noise.
